title: Same fence, same pen?
hook: Bend 20 m of fence into different rectangles. Does every pen hold the same?

knows: perimeter as the distance around a shape
area of a rectangle as width × height
doesNotKnow: that a fixed perimeter fixes neither the shape nor the area of a rectangle

misconception: The same length of fence always encloses the same area; or a long thin pen holds more.
objective: The learner can explain that with w + h fixed at 10, the area w × (10 − w) peaks at 25 for the 5 × 5 square and falls by the square of the distance from 5.

claims.text: A rectangle w by h uses w + h + w + h of fence, so 20 m of fence means w + h = 10.
claims.source: Perimeter of a rectangle = 2(w + h). Demo.tsx FENCE = 20, HALF = FENCE / 2.

claims.text: With 20 m of fence the pens hold 1 × 9 = 9, 2 × 8 = 16, 3 × 7 = 21, 4 × 6 = 24 and 5 × 5 = 25 square metres (and the same again for 6 × 4 down to 9 × 1).
claims.source: area(w) = w × (10 − w) in Demo.tsx, recomputed in node for w = 1..9: 9, 16, 21, 24, 25, 24, 21, 16, 9.

claims.text: Moving d metres away from the square costs d² square metres: the area is 25 minus the square of the distance from 5.
claims.source: w(10 − w) = 25 − (w − 5)² (expand both sides: 10w − w² = 25 − w² + 10w − 25). The reveal quotes the learner's visited width nearest 5.

claims.text: For a fixed length of fence, the square pen holds the most of any rectangle.
claims.source: With w + h = P/2, w·h = (P/4)² − (w − P/4)² ≤ (P/4)², equality only at w = h (AM-GM). Rectangles only; a circle would hold more.

claims.text: Each small grid square is 1 m², so the area is the number of squares inside the fence.
claims.source: Definition of area in square metres; the stage draws a 1 m grid (U px per metre in Demo.tsx).

recall.question: You have 40 m of fence for a rectangular pen. Which holds the most?
recall.why: Width plus height is 20. The square 10 × 10 = 100 m² beats 5 × 15 = 75 and 1 × 19 = 19.
